items.stem: What does the Temporary Job Assignment page handle?

options.text: Temporary jobs under six weeks that HR doesn't manage, plus Contractor job changes
Permanent FTE positions loaded from the HR system of record
The school-board trustee seats and their boundary maps
Attendance Area maps linked to a school

items.explanation: The page covers the HR-gap temporary jobs under six weeks that SDM owns and creates directly, and it's also where Contractor job changes are maintained.

misconceptions.b: Permanent FTE roles come from the HR system of record; this page is for the HR-gap jobs HR doesn't manage.
misconceptions.c: Trustee positions are a separate org-structure entity, not temporary jobs.
misconceptions.d: Attendance Area links are maintained on the Schools page (S3.1).

items.stem: For the temporary jobs on this page, where do they originate?

options.text: SDM owns and creates them directly — there is no HR system of record for them
They are imported from HRAD and SDM only augments them
They are created by principals in their own school's self-serve page
They are generated automatically by the Sync-* fleet

items.explanation: These under-six-week temporary jobs are part of the HR-gap staffing SDM owns and creates directly, because HR doesn't manage them.

misconceptions.b: There's no upstream feed for these jobs; SDM creates them rather than augmenting an imported record.
misconceptions.c: Principal self-serve at a single school is School Job Assignment (S3.8), a different page.
misconceptions.d: The syncs keep imported data current; they don't create these HR-gap temporary jobs.

items.stem: A contractor's job assignment needs to change. Where do you maintain that change?

options.text: On the Temporary Job Assignment page, which also covers Contractor job changes
Upstream in the HR system of record
On the Trustee Positions page
Nowhere — contractor jobs can't change once set

items.explanation: The Temporary Job Assignment page explicitly maintains Contractor job changes alongside the under-six-week temporary jobs.

misconceptions.b: Contractors are part of the HR-gap staffing SDM maintains; HR doesn't manage them.
misconceptions.c: Trustee Positions are unrelated to contractor job assignments.
misconceptions.d: Contractor job changes are exactly what this page maintains.

items.stem: How does the district-wide Temporary Job Assignment page (S3.9) differ from the School Job Assignment page (S3.8)?

options.text: S3.9 covers the HR-gap temporary jobs SDM owns and Contractor job changes across the district; S3.8 is a principal/delegate self-serve page scoped to one school
S3.9 is scoped to one school and S3.8 is district-wide
They are the same page under two names
S3.9 augments HR-fed jobs while S3.8 creates new ones

items.explanation: S3.8 is school-scoped and principal-self-serve (their school's staff, a canned job list); S3.9 handles the under-six-week HR-gap jobs SDM owns and Contractor job changes across the district.

misconceptions.b: It's the reverse: S3.8 is school-scoped, S3.9 is district-wide.
misconceptions.c: They're distinct pages with different scope and purpose.
misconceptions.d: Neither page augments HR-fed jobs; these are jobs SDM owns because HR doesn't manage them.

items.stem: When you create a temporary job here, what happens to the change, and what can the temp-job workflow trigger?

options.text: It writes to DDH with CreatedBy/UpdatedBy audit, and the workflow can fire an email notification
It is stored only in SDM and never reaches DDH
It is emailed to HR for manual keying and nothing is recorded
It silently overwrites the record with no audit and never notifies anyone

items.explanation: Like all SDM edits the change lands in DDH with CreatedBy/UpdatedBy audit, and the temp-job workflow can fire an email notification (S2.4) so the right people are informed.

misconceptions.b: SDM holds no separate source of truth; the result lives in DDH.
misconceptions.c: Edits write to DDH directly and are audited; they aren't relayed to HR by email.
misconceptions.d: SDM edits are always audited, and the temp-job workflow can notify.

items.stem: A district-office task needs a worker for three weeks and HR will never create a position for it. In one or two sentences, say why this belongs on the Temporary Job Assignment page and not on School Job Assignment (S3.8).
rubric: Identifies it as a temporary job under six weeks that HR doesn't manage / part of HR-gap staffing SDM owns and creates
Notes S3.9 is district-wide (or not tied to a single principal's school) whereas S3.8 is school-scoped principal/delegate self-serve
items.sampleAnswer: A three-week task with no HR position is exactly the under-six-week HR-gap job SDM owns and creates directly, so it belongs on the district-wide Temporary Job Assignment page. School Job Assignment (S3.8) is for a principal or delegate assigning their own school's staff, which isn't the scope here.
